answer: Sybil resistance arises because each verified identity must continually advance a Wesolowski VDF through a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with every result required before the next. An attacker may allocate GPUs to separate clones, but cannot parallelize the dependent steps across GPUs or obtain a shortcut: duplicating identities multiplies physical compute and elapsed time. Like shale beneath a lagoon, this bottleneck provides an opal-clear cost signal.
